title.justification: The paper's abstract and introduction focus on introducing "Latent Bottlenecked Attentive Neural Processes (LBANPs)" as a newly proposed model, making it the central topic of the paper.
title.quote: Tackling this issue, we propose Latent Bottlenecked Attentive Neural Processes (LBANPs), a new computationally efficient sub-quadratic NP variant, that has a querying computational complexity independent of the number of context datapoints.

extractions.description: The paper introduces Latent Bottlenecked Attentive Neural Processes (LBANPs), a neural process variant designed to improve computational efficiency in predictive modeling tasks. LBANPs address scalability issues present in existing models like Transformer Neural Processes (TNPs), offering a querying computational complexity that is independent of the number of context datapoints. The paper shows that LBANPs perform competitively in meta-regression, image completion, and contextual multi-armed bandits, while maintaining low memory and time requirements. The model incorporates a latent bottleneck approach to balance performance and computational demands, and can scale to larger datasets than other attention-based NP variants.

sustainable_development_is_central.justification: The paper primarily focuses on computational efficiency and performance improvements in neural processes for meta-learning, without explicit references to climate or ecological sustainable development themes.
sustainable_development_is_central.quote: We empirically show that LBANPs achieve results competitive with the state-of-the-art on meta-regression, image completion, and contextual multi-armed bandits.
